name: host-guards-block-attribution-and-cjk
title: Make both host PreToolUse guards block attribution trailers and non-English commits from one shared predicate
description: Two generated PreToolUse guards, one per host (.claude/hooks for the Claude host, .codex/hooks for the Codex host), must block rather than warn: (1) a new attribution guard that exits 2 when a git commit command carries an AI-host attribution trailer (Co-Authored-By naming a host or the noreply@anthropic.com address, a Claude-Session or Codex-Session line, or the Generated with footer); (2) the existing english-only-guard converted from warn-only to exit 2 on CJK in guarded commands, and added to the Codex roster where getCodexHooks() currently registers no English guard at all. Both hosts share one predicate source kept byte-equivalent by a keep-in-sync test, and the host-neutral git-level .githooks/commit-msg stays as the fallback for commits no PreToolUse hook can see (CLI auto-commits, human commits). Every checklist item carries an explicit RED (a check that fails on main today) and GREEN (the same check passing after the fix), and red_evidence_create binds each RED before its fix lands. Motivation: the user rule that no AI-host attribution enters git history was re-broken by every new session because the harness re-injects the trailer instruction; only a mechanical guard that travels with the clone (host hook files are tracked in git, core.hooksPath is not) can hold it.
